niche: Human psychology and behavior: body language, eye contact, persuasion, memory, habits, decision making, cognitive biases and everyday social dynamics.
audience: English-speaking viewers, mostly in the US, aged 16-45, who like quick surprising explanations they can use in daily life.
tone: Intriguing, confident and conversational. Short punchy sentences. Speak to the viewer as 'you'.
topic_ideas: Why you cannot stop checking your phone
The anchoring effect that makes you overpay
Why your brain remembers embarrassing moments forever
What the mere-exposure effect does to your taste
Why we procrastinate even when we know the cost
rules: Only use well-established, widely replicated findings (for example anchoring, confirmation bias, the mere-exposure effect, loss aversion).
Never give a precise statistic or study result unless it is real and widely documented; otherwise phrase it carefully ('research suggests').
Never diagnose anyone, never give medical or mental-health treatment advice.
Frame persuasion and manipulation tactics as awareness (how to notice them), not as instructions to exploit people.
avoid: pop-psychology myths (left-brain/right-brain, only 10% of the brain, learning styles)
